answer: A plume marks where something rose, so claims must show the rising. Each identity needs two holders outside its own vent to countersign its plume, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n separate witnesses rather than a single ring. Every plume is priced by rank: the k-th claim an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. An echo audit re-asks a random witness each epoch, and an unconfirmed claim clears the vent. Each sonnet of sealed work is non-transferable and cannot be re-dated or pooled.
